_comment: Suggested sweep ranges for step C optimisation — calibrate after A2 noise analysis

noise.gaussian_std.rationale: Industrial 8-bit cameras: 3–6 DN quiet, 10–15 DN noisy. BinaryThreshold=80 means noise < half-threshold is safe; beyond ~15 DN the threshold starts eating real detections.
noise.gaussian_std.calibrate_from_A2: measure std-dev of a static background region across frames

noise.reflection_brightness.rationale: 0 = ideal, 80 = near threshold (80 DN). At 80 reflections start generating false contours. Realistic lab setups are usually 20–45 DN.
noise.reflection_brightness.calibrate_from_A2: find brightest static blob that does not move between frames

noise.n_reflections.rationale: Each reflection is a potential false positive. Up to 4 is typical for an overhead single-lamp setup; 7 tests robustness.
noise.n_reflections.calibrate_from_A2: count bright stable blobs in background frame

noise.temporal_flicker_std.rationale: LED panels: ≤1 DN. Fluorescent/mains-coupled lighting: 3–6 DN at 10 fps due to 50/100 Hz beat. Affects BackgroundSubtraction stability.
noise.temporal_flicker_std.calibrate_from_A2: measure per-frame mean brightness over an empty arena region

animal.semi_major_px.rationale: At ~1.72 px/mm (1280 px width): 25 px ≈ 14 mm (small insect), 70 px ≈ 40 mm (large fish). ContourAreaFilter max_area=300000 is not the binding constraint; min_area=7 means even 25 px semi-major is fine.
animal.semi_major_px.calibrate_from_A2: measure contour bounding-box of real animals in debug images

animal.semi_minor_px.comment: derive from semi_major and desired aspect ratio

animal.round_radius_px.rationale: 15 px ≈ 9 mm (beetle), 45 px ≈ 26 mm (snail). Keep area < 300000 px² i.e. radius < 309 px.

animal.gray_value.rationale: Floor ~182 DN. Contrast = floor_gray - gray_value must exceed BinaryThreshold=80 after BackgroundSubtraction produces a difference frame. At gray_value=110 the contrast is 72 DN — below threshold; start the sweep here to intentionally stress the pipeline. At gray_value=30 contrast is 152 DN — very easy detection.
animal.gray_value.calibrate_from_A2: measure animal pixel intensity in raw frames

trajectory.speed_px.rationale: At 10 fps: 3 px/f ≈ 1.7 mm/s (slow crawl), 22 px/f ≈ 13 mm/s (fast fish). Fast movement causes MOG2 foreground mask smearing; tune BinaryThreshold or MorphologyClose kernel accordingly.
trajectory.speed_px.calibrate_from_A2: measure frame-to-frame centroid displacement from mass_center debug images

trajectory.turn_std_deg.rationale: 5 deg = directed swimmer (fish), 40 deg = thigmotactic random walk (insect hugging wall). Higher turn std produces more complex trajectories that expose tracking gaps.

pipeline.binary_threshold.rationale: This is the primary sensitivity knob in pipe-default-42. Lower = more false positives, higher = missed detections. Sweep together with animal.gray_value.
pipeline.binary_threshold.note: Change 'threshold' field in BinaryThreshold_CUDA step of pipeline JSON

pipeline.morph_ksize.rationale: MorphologyClose fills gaps in the foreground mask. Larger kernel = more gap-filling but also merges nearby objects. Default=15.

pipeline.contour_max_contours.rationale: 0 = legacy behaviour (all contours merged, centroid smear possible). 1 = largest-area contour wins — eliminates smear when a reflection and animal coexist in the frame. Should almost always be 1 in production; sweep [0,1] to quantify how much smear costs in terms of alpha and eta.
pipeline.contour_max_contours.note: Change 'max_contours' field in ContourAreaFilter_CUDA step. Source: area_filter_count metadata key tracks frames where >1 contour passed the area gate (eta metric).

pipeline.contour_min_area.rationale: Filters noise contours. Raising from 7 to 500 eliminates camera noise false positives at the cost of missing very small animals.
